# Read-back

A swim squad of twelve people divided into three groups (sprint, middle distance, distance) run a 150-minute practice session across three lanes with one coach on deck and one set of starting blocks. The morning flows through on-deck briefing and observation, a synchronized warm-up in all three lanes, a whiteboard strategy talk, a kick set (mixed equipment), main sets that run in parallel but at different durations per lane (each lane's work is variable: 30–50 minutes, with 40/45/50 as targets), a sprint set that must serialize across lanes using the single shared block set (10 minutes per lane, three lanes total, times taken by the coach), a synchronized cool-down once every lane clears the blocks, and a final on-deck debrief. The constraints are: three lanes (run in parallel), one set of starting blocks (forces serialization of sprint work), one coach (watches and times from the deck), and a hard stop at 150 minutes of pool time. The main set is the only phase with built-in variability; everything else is either synchronized or serialized. The text is complete.
